Method of Attack: Used by North Korean hackers to steal files and send them to Google Drive storage

Backdoor malware with capabilities including stealing information from web browsers (passwords), taking screenshots, logging keystrokes, scanning local and removable drives, stealing files from connected phones, lowering Google account security settings
Uses Google Drive as command and control (C2) server and to store stolen files
Establishes persistence by modifying Windows Registry
Commands delivered via Google Drive uploads, results uploaded back
Uses multi-step XOR-decryption, process creation, and execution of payload in memory
Exploited Internet Explorer vulnerability in watering-hole attack
Impacted Systems: Connected phones via Windows Portable Device API
Attack Vector: Watering-hole attack exploiting Internet Explorer vulnerability
Indicators of Compromise: Hashes for Dolphin backdoor versions 1.9 through 3.0 (86/64-bit) provided by ESET
Use of Google Drive for C2 and data exfiltration
